lines.japanese: 「どしたの、委員長」
lines.english: “What’s up, class rep?”

lines.japanese: 目的もなく廊下へ向かおうとした一限目の終わり、渡来さんが声をかけてきてくれた。そういえばここ数日、休み時間にあまり廊下へ出ていない。
lines.english: At the end of first period, I was heading aimlessly into the hallway when Watarai called to me. Come to think of it, I had hardly gone out there during breaks these past few days.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君の遅刻って珍しいよね。なに、きのう夜更かししたの」
lines.english: “It’s rare for you to be late, Haneda. What happened, were you up late last night?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあちょっとね」
lines.english: “Yes. A little.”

lines.japanese: 「デートか」
lines.english: “A date?”

lines.japanese: 「や、まさか、相手は男の子だよ」
lines.english: “No, nothing like that. It was a boy.”

lines.japanese: 「あれれ。もしかして、ほんとに誰かと出かけてた？」
lines.english: “Oh? Were you actually out with someone?”

lines.japanese: うーん、ＲＰＧも知らない渡来さんにメタバースって言っても分からないよなあ。
lines.english: Hmm. Watarai didn't even know what an RPG was. She wasn't going to understand ‘metaverse.’

lines.japanese: 「ええと、ちょっと今日の放課後にひとと会う約束してるんだけど、そのひととまあ」
lines.english: “Well, I’m meeting someone after school today, and he and I were...”

lines.japanese: 僕は時計を見て確認した。今日の放課後の約束が楽しみだ。
lines.english: I checked the clock. I was looking forward to our meeting that afternoon.

lines.japanese: 「デートってことは女の子だ？」
lines.english: “So it is a date, and she’s a girl?”

lines.japanese: 「あの……おれの話聞いてる？　だからね、最近知りあった男の子がいて……」
lines.english: “Um... are you listening to me? I’m saying I met this boy recently...”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、ゲーム繋がり？」
lines.english: “Through games?”

lines.japanese: 「んー……いや、音楽かな」
lines.english: “Hmm... No. Music, I suppose.”

lines.japanese: アクセントが頭に来ない、平板読みのオンガク。
lines.english: “Music.” I said it flat, without the usual stress up front.

lines.japanese: 隣りにいた鴻野君が僕の顔を見た。そういえば前に彼から好きな音楽を聞かれて、いくつか知っている声優のヒット曲を勧めた記憶がある。
lines.english: Kono beside me looked at my face. Come to think of it, he'd once asked what music I liked, and I'd recommended a few hit songs by voice actors I knew.

lines.japanese: もしかして、ずっと音楽通だと思われていたのかもしれない。やあ。軽く頭を下げかえしておいた。
lines.english: Perhaps he had mistaken me for a connoisseur all this time. Hello. I returned his look with a shallow bow.

lines.japanese: 「音楽だあ。羽田君ってどんな音楽聞くの？」
lines.english: “Music, huh? What kind do you listen to, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、インディーズのバンドだから渡来さんは知らないと思う。もう解散してるしコアなファンばっかりなんだ。知るひとぞ知るって感じでね」
lines.english: “It’s an indie band, so I doubt you’ve heard of them. They’ve already broken up, and only the really hardcore fans are left. They’re one of those bands for people in the know.”

lines.japanese: また鴻野君が僕を見た。やあ。もう一度頭を下げかえしておいた。
lines.english: Kono looked at me again. Hello. I acknowledged him with another shallow bow.

lines.japanese: 「え、なんかかっこいいじゃん。私にも教えてよ。なんてバンド？」
lines.english: “That sounds kind of cool. Tell me about them. What are they called?”

lines.japanese: 「言っても分からないと思うよ。『ロックバード』って言うんだけど」
lines.english: “You probably won’t know them. They’re called Rockbird.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　もしかして知ってた？」
lines.english: “What? Have you heard of them?”

lines.japanese: あ、そうか。よく考えたら、もともと僕がロックバードの名前を検索かけて調べたのは、渡来さんが友達との会話でその固有名詞を口にしていたからだったっけ。
lines.english: Oh, right. Thinking about it, I'd originally searched Rockbird's name because Watarai had said it while talking with a friend, hadn't I?

lines.japanese: でもいまの渡来さんは明らかに興味のなさそうな顔をしてる。ああいうヴィジュアル系ロックは好みじゃなさそうだもんな。僕と同じ感じで、なんとなく名前は知ってるぐらいの認識度なのかな。
lines.english: But Watarai obviously looked bored now. Guess that kind of showy, theatrical rock wasn't her thing. Maybe she was like me and just sort of knew the name?

lines.japanese: あ、そうだ。だけど僕はとっておきの情報を持ってる。これを知ったら彼女もちょっと驚くんじゃないかと思う。
lines.english: Oh, right. I had a really good piece of trivia. I bet she'd be a little surprised when she heard it.

lines.japanese: 「実はね、そこのボーカルって、いま人気の御影クリヤだったんだ」
lines.english: “Actually, their vocalist was Kuriya Mikage—you know, the singer who’s popular now.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、栗山君でしょ？」
lines.english: “Oh, you mean Kuriyama.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、栗山じゃなくて御影クリヤだよ。え、もしかして知らないのかな御影クリヤ。いま音楽番組とかにもよく出てるんだけど」
lines.english: “No, not Kuriyama. Kuriya Mikage. Wait, have you really never heard of Kuriya Mikage? He’s on music shows all the time now.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、栗山君でしょ？」
lines.english: “That’s what I said. Kuriyama.”

lines.japanese: どうやら彼女は別のひとと勘違いしているらしい。うーん、意外と芸能関係にうといのかな。
lines.english: Looks like she had him mixed up with somebody else. Hmm. Maybe she was surprisingly out of touch with celebrities.

lines.japanese: 「先ぱーい、羽田君がロックバードのファンなんだってー」
lines.english: “Hariu! Haneda says he’s a Rockbird fan!”

lines.japanese: 針生さんの口がわずかに動いた。へえ、針生さんもロックバードを知ってたんだ。
lines.english: Hariu’s mouth moved faintly. So he knew Rockbird too.

lines.japanese: そうだ、もしかしてそれをきっかけに仲良くなれるかもしれない。僕は針生さんにもとっておきの情報を教えてあげることにした。
lines.english: Maybe this could help us become friends. I decided to tell Hariu my special bit of trivia too.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん、実は御影クリヤってロックバードのボーカルだったんですよ」
lines.english: “Hariu, did you know Kuriya Mikage used to sing for Rockbird?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、栗山な」
lines.english: “Yeah. Kuriyama.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、栗山じゃなくて御影クリヤですよ」
lines.english: “No, not Kuriyama. Kuriya Mikage.”

lines.japanese: 「だから栗山だろ？」
lines.english: “That’s what I said, isn’t it? Kuriyama.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんも勘違いしているみたいだ。彼はいかにも音楽通な感じがするけど、だからこそ逆に邦楽なんか聴かないぜ、っていうタイプなのかもしれない。
lines.english: Looks like Hariu had him mixed up too. He looked like such a music buff, though. Maybe that was exactly why he was the type to go, ‘Japanese music? I don't listen to that stuff.’

lines.japanese: 針生さんは相変わらずどこか億劫そうに座っている。ただ、今はその視線の先に渡来さんがいた。
lines.english: Hariu sat as languidly as ever. At that moment, however, his gaze rested on Watarai.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんも無言で針生さんに微笑を向けている。目と目の会話。何だろう、なんとなく胸が痛くなった。
lines.english: Watarai returned his look with a silent smile. A conversation between their eyes. For some reason, my chest began to ache.

lines.japanese: そうだ、次の授業が始まるまでにトイレへ行っておかないと。僕は二人の視界を遮らないよう、こっそり廊下へ踏みだした。
lines.english: Oh, right. I needed to use the bathroom before next class. I quietly stepped into the hall, making sure not to get between them.

lines.japanese: 尿意がないままトイレに向かうのはいつものことだ。僕は壁に寄りかかって、フロアの奥まで続く廊下を見つめた。
lines.english: Going to the restroom without any need to use it was a habit of mine. I leaned against the wall and gazed down the corridor to the far end of the floor.

lines.japanese: このフロアの一番奥にはＨ組がある。森里君は入院してると聞いたけど、様子はどうなんだろう。Ｈ組へ行けば誰かお見舞いに行った人がいるかもしれない。
lines.english: Class H was at the very end. I had heard Morisato was in the hospital. How was he doing? Someone in his class might have visited him.

lines.japanese: 休み時間の残りを確認して、早足でＨ組に向かってみた。
lines.english: I checked how much of the break remained, then hurried toward Class H.

lines.japanese: Ｈ組の前に来ると、教室のドアは開いていた。森里君の席に鞄はかかっていない。
lines.english: When I arrived, the classroom door stood open. No schoolbag hung from Morisato’s desk.

lines.japanese: その代わりに、机の上に菊の花が置いてあった。クラスの誰かが快復を祈ってお見舞い代わりに置いてくれたのかな。
lines.english: Instead, there was a chrysanthemum on his desk. Maybe someone in his class had put it there instead of a get-well gift, hoping he'd get better.

lines.japanese: 「やあ」
lines.english: “Hello.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　おま、誰だっけ、この前も来たじゃん」
lines.english: “Huh? You—who were you again? You came by before, didn’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、羽田。羽田鷹志。森里和馬君の友達なんだ」
lines.english: “Haneda. Takashi Haneda. I’m a friend of Kazuma Morisato.”

lines.japanese: 「おーっ！　羽田クンじゃん、なに、また森里クンに会いに来たの？」
lines.english: “Oh! It’s Haneda! What, did you come to see Morisato again?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。だっておれと森里君は友達だからね」
lines.english: “Yes. Morisato and I are friends, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「カッケーわ、羽田クン、マジカッケーわ。こりゃ森里クンも喜ぶわ」
lines.english: “That’s cool, Haneda. Seriously, that’s so cool. Morisato’s gonna love this.”

lines.japanese: 「なになに、どしたん。あ、コレが噂の羽田クン？」
lines.english: “What, what’s going on? Oh, is this that Haneda everybody’s talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「噂のじゃねーッつの、おまえも一年ンとき同じクラスだろ。忘れてンじゃねーよ、こんなカックイー羽田クンをよ」
lines.english: “What do you mean, ‘that Haneda’? You were in his class in first year too. Don’t tell me you forgot somebody as cool as Haneda here.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう。ところで誰か、森里君のお見舞いに行ったひとはいないかな」
lines.english: “Thank you. By the way, has anyone visited Morisato in the hospital?”

lines.japanese: 「あア？　あー、お見舞いねえ……あれ、羽田クン行ってないの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, a hospital visit... Wait, you haven’t gone, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「だっておれ、入院先知らないからさ」
lines.english: “I don’t know which hospital he’s in.”

lines.japanese: 「てことはアレだ。果物とか持って、ご挨拶に行きたいんだ」
lines.english: “So you want to bring him some fruit and pay him a visit.”

lines.japanese: 「もちろんだよ。きっと机にお花が置いてあるって知ったら、森里君も喜ぶんじゃないかな」
lines.english: “Of course. I’m sure Morisato will be glad when he hears somebody left flowers on his desk.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ？　なにソレ？」
lines.english: “Huh? What’s that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese: 「え、だってあそこ、森里君の机に快復祈願の花が――」
lines.english: “What? There’s a flower on Morisato’s desk to pray for his recovery—”

lines.japanese: 「……ッ！　……ッッ、……ッ！　やべ、ツボッた……！」
lines.english: “...! ...Ngh—! Oh man, that got me...!”

lines.japanese: 「クハッ……！　こりゃキツイっすわ……！　腹痛ェ……痛い痛い、マジ痛い……！」
lines.english: “Khh...! That’s brutal...! My stomach—ow, ow, it seriously hurts...!”

lines.japanese: 僕が森里君の机を指差すと、急にふたりはお腹を抱えてしまった。
lines.english: When I pointed to Morisato’s desk, both boys abruptly doubled over clutching their stomachs.

lines.japanese: そのとき、残念ながら授業開始のベルが鳴ってしまった。僕の教室は一番端だから、急いで戻らないといけない。
lines.english: Unfortunately, the bell rang for the start of class. My classroom was at the opposite end of the floor; I had to hurry.

lines.japanese: 「あっ！　じゃあおれ教室に戻るよ。また今度来てもいいかな」
lines.english: “Oh! I have to get back to class. May I come by again sometime?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、涙出てきた。はいはい、またきてね羽田クン」
lines.english: “Ah, I’m crying. Sure, sure. Come back anytime, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「森里クンが来たら教えてやるから。じゃーねー、まったねー」
lines.english: “We’ll tell Morisato you stopped by when he comes back. See you around.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう！」
lines.english: “Thank you!”

lines.japanese: 僕は何度か振りかえりながら教室へ向かった。早く森里君が良くなって、学校でまた会えたらいいなと思う。
lines.english: I looked back several times on the way to my classroom. I hoped Morisato recovered soon and that I could see him at school again.

lines.japanese: 「それでは今から解説を始めるので、答案を机の上に出してください」
lines.english: “I’m going to explain the answers now, so please place your tests on your desks.”

lines.japanese: 今日からテストの返却が始まった。恩田先生が担当教科を務める英語の結果は、８６点という高得点をマークすることが出来た。
lines.english: Our exams began coming back that day. In English, Ms. Onda’s subject, I had earned a strong score of eighty-six.

lines.japanese: 僕は携帯電話を開いて、残務処理のひとつ“３：期末テストで平均７０点以上とる”を確認した。
lines.english: I opened my phone and checked one item of unfinished business: “3. Average at least seventy on the final exams.”

lines.japanese: 今回の目標は平均点７０点台だ。苦手教科の理数系をカバーするには、１６点というアドバンテージはかなり大きい。それでも少しでも点数が上がればと、恩田先生の解答と自分の答案を照らし合わせた。
lines.english: My target was an average somewhere in the seventies. A sixteen-point cushion would go a long way toward compensating for my weak math and science subjects. Still hoping to recover another point or two, I compared Ms. Onda’s answers with my test.

lines.japanese: 結局、恩田先生の採点に間違いはなく、僕の点数は８６点で確定した。今回のテストは割と簡単だった気がする。最後の期末だからある程度楽にしてくれたのかもしれない。
lines.english: In the end, Ms. Onda had made no mistake. My score was fixed at eighty-six. The exam had seemed fairly easy. Perhaps the teachers had gone easy on us because these were our last finals.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君～、今回難しくなかった？　ちょっと気が緩んじゃってたのかもね」
lines.english: “Haneda, wasn’t this one hard? Maybe I let my guard down a little.”

lines.japanese: どうやら難易度は普段と変わらなかったらしい。渡来さんが傾きながら僕の机にやってきた。
lines.english: Apparently it had been no easier than usual. Watarai came over to my desk at a slant.

lines.japanese: 「おれは初日に力を発揮するみたい。そんなに悪くなかったよ」
lines.english: “I seem to perform best on the first day. I didn’t do too badly.”

lines.japanese: 「具体的に何点？」
lines.english: “So what’d you get?”

lines.japanese: 「８６点。最後の読解を間違えなければ、あと４点プラスされたのにな。渡来さんはどうだったの？」
lines.english: “Eighty-six. If I hadn’t missed the final reading question, I’d have gotten another four points. How did you do?”

lines.japanese: 「ほー、やるねえ羽田君。ははは、だが次はこうはいかないぞ！　覚えておくがいい！」
lines.english: “Oho, nicely done, Haneda. Hahaha! But next time will be different! Remember that!”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　もしかして良くなかったの？」
lines.english: “What? Did you do badly?”

lines.japanese: 「良くなくはないけど、羽田君よりは良くない」
lines.english: “Not badly. Just not as well as you.”

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃあいいじゃない。何点だったのか教えてよ」
lines.english: “Then you did fine. Tell me your score.”

lines.japanese: 「だけど羽田君に負けるのは悔しいから言いたくない」
lines.english: “I don’t want to. It’s frustrating to lose to you.”

lines.japanese: 「な、何だよそれー。なんでおれに負けるのは嫌なんだよ……」
lines.english: “Wh-what’s that supposed to mean? Why is losing to me so terrible...?”

lines.japanese: 「だって私、羽田君しか見せる相手いないもん」
lines.english: “Because you’re the only person I have to show it to.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: どうしてそんなことを言うんだろう。渡来さんは他にも仲のいい友達が沢山いると思うんだけどな。
lines.english: Why would she say that? I thought Watarai had lots of close friends.

lines.japanese: 「でもそんなことで悔しがるなんて、もしかして渡来さんってわりと負けず嫌い？」
lines.english: “If it bothers you this much, are you actually pretty competitive?”

lines.japanese: 「てゆか羽田君こそ負けず嫌いじゃん」
lines.english: “You’re the competitive one, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんで。どうしておれが」
lines.english: “Wh-why? What makes you say that?”

lines.japanese: 「だっていま負けず嫌いだって言われて悔しそうだもん」
lines.english: “Because you look annoyed that I called you competitive.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なにその論理。渡来さん子供みたいだよ」
lines.english: “What kind of logic is that? You’re acting like a child.”

lines.japanese: ていうか、つまり彼女は僕をからかいに来たのか。あはは、森里君みたいだ。軽口を叩ける仲っていうのは友達の証拠みたいなものだから、ちょっと嬉しくなってしまう。
lines.english: So she had come over just to tease me? Ahaha. She was like Morisato. Being close enough to trade jabs was practically proof of friendship, and the thought made me a little happy.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、今回は痛み分けってことでいいのかな」
lines.english: “Well, shall we call this one even?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、もしかして痛み分けって言葉を間違えてないかな。あのね、この場合渡来さんが一方的に負けたわけだから、痛み分けっていう言葉は適さないんだよ」
lines.english: “Wait, I think you’re using ‘even’ wrong. You lost all by yourself, so this is not what anyone would call even.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、もしかしてさっきの怒ってる？　そんな揚げ足とるみたいに」
lines.english: “Wait, are you angry about what I said? You’re really splitting hairs now.”

lines.japanese: 「ははは、今回で言えば、渡来さんの一人相撲だよ」
lines.english: “Hahaha. You were competing with yourself, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「うるさいよ」
lines.english: “Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それで結局何点だったの？」
lines.english: “So what did you score in the end?”

lines.japanese: 「絶対教えない」
lines.english: “I’m never telling you.”

lines.japanese: 「負けず嫌いだなあ」
lines.english: “You really are competitive.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは何かとんでもないものを見たような表情を浮かべると、テストを胸に抱きながら自分の席に戻っていった。彼女の両腕に包まれたその紙切れがちょっとうらやましいなと思った。
lines.english: Watarai looked like she'd seen something unbelievable, hugged the test to her chest, and went back to her seat. I felt a little jealous of that piece of paper in her arms.
